messages:
Rina Kobayashi: ok folks — quick async review on final report outline for FP8/INT8 sprint. what tables/plots do we want + how do we phrase recs so it's defensible? aiming to publish to Confluence tomorrow. I have a draft outline but want eyes esp on “what counts as success” + the right way to present tradeoffs.

Rina Kobayashi: current sections:
1) exec summary (1 page)
2) methodology + environment pins
3) results (end-to-end)
4) microbench + kernel attribution
5) scheduler experiments
6) correctness/quality guardrails
7) recommendations + rollout plan
8) follow-ups / open questions

Noah Patel: +1 on structure. for tables/plots, I’d make sure we have:
- “headline” table: per (model_family, GPU, quant_mode) => baseline vs optimized deltas for TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, tok/s, and cost proxy. keep it to 8–12 rows (top hosted only), push the full matrix to appendix.
- plot: TTFT p95 delta vs TPOT p95 delta scatter (so we can show the tail tradeoff from scheduler caps).
- plot: breakdown bars for prefill vs decode time (end-to-end), split by quant mode.

Grace Kim: re: microbench, I’d include one “kernel timeline” figure per GPU (H100 vs A100 behave differently). but keep it as *illustrative*, not “we proved this with Nsight” lol.
Also a table that shows chosen kernel family distribution (% of requests choosing FP8 attn kernel A vs B), because auto-selector changes are part of the story.

Hiro Tanaka: agree. also need a clear “what changed” table mapping PRs -> expected impact area.
Something like:
- PR 10622 (FP8 attn tuning): prefill speedup on H100/H200
- PR 10623 (INT8 GEMM fusion): decode tok/s improvement
- PR 10624 (scheduler batch cap): tail latency improvement on mixed workloads
- PR 10625 (auto-selector bug): correctness + perf stability
…and then link to full list in appendix.

Sofia Ivanova: for scheduler experiments, please show both:
1) mixed prompt-length workload (prefill-heavy + decode-heavy)
2) streaming chat scenario (TTFT/TPOT)
We keep getting questions like “you improved TPOT but TTFT regressed” so the report needs to say: this policy is *only enabled for quantized decode* / when queue depth is high, etc.
Maybe a heatmap: batch cap vs concurrency => p95 TPOT.

Allison Grant: dashboard/observability angle: add 1 screenshot-style mock panel (or at least the query) showing the tags we’re going to rely on: model, gpu_sku, runtime_commit, quant_mode, kernel_id.
Also recommend one plot for “queue wait time histogram” pre/post scheduler change (it’s intuitive).

Connor O'Brien: phrasing: avoid “we recommend enabling FP8 everywhere” language.
I’d frame as:
- “Recommended defaults (safe)”
- “Opt-in knobs (requires validation)”
- “Known caveats / when to fall back to FP16”
And explicitly call out gating: what regressions will block the release train vs allowed with allowlist + mitigation.

Talia Benson: +1. exec summary should have 3 bullets max:
- what we measured
- what improved (numbers)
- what we’re shipping now + what’s next
Also add a “how to reproduce” callout box (commands + where results artifacts live).

Sean Gallagher: please add 2 sentences on perf lab reliability + what we did to reduce noise (pinned container digest, locked clocks, dedicated nodes). otherwise people will question variance.
If possible, one mini-table: run-to-run variance baseline (e.g., CV) for 2 representative tests.

Arjun Desai: correctness section: we need a small table that’s basically “drift checks summary”.
Columns: model family, quant mode, eval set (sanity prompts), max abs delta (logprob) or pass/fail, fallback triggers.
We don’t need to oversell it, but need to show “we didn’t just chase perf.”

Priyanka Bose: also add a callout: “accuracy-sensitive layers / known risky configs” (e.g., long-context prefill + FP8 alignment issue that we fixed). It can be a short bullet list with “mitigation: pin runtime >= X / disable kernel on L40S” etc.

Julian Moore: for the instrumentation bits, add one plot showing request phase spans (prefill/decode) w/ quant_mode tag. even if it’s a single screenshot from the trace UI, it helps justify attribution.

Mateo Alvarez: on recommendations language: make sure we separate “what the data says” from “what we’re choosing to do.”
Suggested template for each recommendation:
- Finding (with metric + confidence)
- Proposed change (default/knob)
- Risk + mitigations
- Rollout plan (canary cohort, rollback)
This reads well for leadership + Release Eng.

Rina Kobayashi: this is great. I’m going to incorporate:
- headline summary table (top models x GPUs only)
- TTFT vs TPOT p95 scatter
- prefill/decode stacked bars
- kernel selection distribution table
- scheduler heatmap (cap vs concurrency) + queue wait histogram
- variance mini-table
- correctness drift summary table
- “what changed” PR mapping table

Rina Kobayashi: wording updates per Connor/Mateo: “safe defaults” vs “opt-in knobs”, and each rec as Finding -> Change -> Risk -> Rollout.

Connor O'Brien: also pls add a one-liner in the exec summary: “All changes ship behind flags; default changes limited to X” so people don’t panic.

Allison Grant: if you want, I can drop in a quick dashboard mock from the spec (panels + tag conventions). just tell me what format you want.

Rina Kobayashi: yes please — screenshot or even just the panel list in text is fine. send in-thread or DM.

Grace Kim: one more: please add an appendix table “anomalies & exclusions” (e.g., noisy L40S run, long-context FP8 regression pre-fix). otherwise reviewers will ask.

Noah Patel: +1. and in the main results section, put “N= runs, median over X, outlier policy” in the caption of every plot. saves a lot of back-and-forth.

Rina Kobayashi: noted. I’ll post updated outline EOD for final :eyes:.

Confluence Bot: Rina Kobayashi updated a page: https://confluence.redwood.local/display/SERVE/Fp8+Int8+Sprint+Report+Draft (last edited 12:41)

Sofia Ivanova: skimmed — looks good. one nit: in scheduler section, please rename “batch cap” -> “quantized decode batch cap” so it’s obvious we’re not touching FP16 path.

Rina Kobayashi: good call, will rename.

Mateo Alvarez: 👍 once it’s updated, ping me + Connor for signoff so we can include in release notes packet.

Rina Kobayashi: will do.
